question: With n measurements on an unseen alloy, does a frozen ML model plus a model update and jackknife+ give better 90% intervals than (a) the existing calibration methods and (b) models built from the target measurements alone?
disclosure: The proposed method family (shift / linear update with jackknife+, zero clip) and the target-only linear baselines were chosen after an exploratory test on 2026-10-22 using the 20 Oct fixed test rows. Exploratory equal-alloy depth interval scores at 9 measurements were: current method + clip 567, ML linear update + clip 402, target-only P+V + clip 411. This run uses 50 fresh, group-aware test draws per alloy and a fixed selection rule. Rows are the same physical records, so this reduces but cannot remove selection bias.

excluded.classification: Reported as a secondary negative result on 20 Oct; known unquarantined unit-error rows 679-681.

partition_rule: Condition groups = identical active model inputs (rounded 1e-9). Groups go wholly to test or pool. Greedy random fill of test to <= 20 rows. Calibration = nested prefixes of one random pool permutation.
models: Unchanged frozen excluded-alloy models, seeds 0-4 (Weeks 1-2 seed 0, Weeks 3-4 refits 1-4).

source_split: Frozen ML point, split conformal on other alloys' reserved calibration rows
target_split: Frozen ML point, split conformal on target residuals (20 Oct Thesis C method)
mean_target_split: Training mean, split conformal on target residuals (20 Oct simple predictor)
target_mean_jk: Target-sample mean, jackknife+ (training mean plus shift update)
target_linPV_jk: Target-only OLS y ~ 1 + P + V, jackknife+
target_auto_jk: Target-only, choose mean / P/V / P+V by inner LOO MSE, jackknife+
ml_shift_jk: Frozen ML plus intercept update r ~ 1, jackknife+
ml_linear_jk: Frozen ML plus intercept and slope update r ~ 1 + p, jackknife+
ml_auto_jk: Frozen ML, choose shift or linear update by inner LOO MSE, jackknife+ (PRIMARY)

selection_rule: Auto methods choose the candidate with the lowest exact LOO MSE on calibration data; ties -> simpler. The choice runs inside every jackknife fold.
physical_bound: Primary results clip lower bounds at 0 for every method (geometry >= 0; coverage cannot fall). Unclipped results are stored as well.
aggregation: Rows -> condition; mean over repeats within (alloy, seed, budget, method); mean over seeds; equal-alloy mean within cohort. Alloy is the unit of analysis.
acceptability: A method is acceptable only if its equal-alloy coverage >= 0.85 (jackknife+ worst case is 0.80).

hypotheses.H_primary: Depth, primary cohort, budget 9, clipped: ml_auto_jk has a lower equal-alloy interval score than target_split (the 20 Oct method). Test: exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on alloy-level differences; with 7 alloys the smallest attainable p is 0.0156.
hypotheses.H_existing: ml_auto_jk beats source_split and target_split at every budget (all tasks). Descriptive + Wilcoxon.
hypotheses.H_baseline: ml_auto_jk beats mean_target_split and target_mean_jk at every budget.
hypotheses.H_prior_value: ml_auto_jk vs target_auto_jk: report the difference by budget; a crossover is allowed and is itself a result. No direction is assumed.

decision_rule_for_superiority: Call ml_auto_jk superior to a comparator on a task and budget only if (1) its equal-alloy interval score is lower, (2) it wins in a majority of alloys, and (3) both coverages are acceptable.
